description: errorMessage is nonstandard — Ajv gets it from the ajv-errors plugin, and jsonschema-validate implements the same portable subset independently by reading the messages out of the schema JSON. An authored message is one of the two texts the wrappers generate rather than the libraries, so the two legs are contracted to emit it identically.

cases.name: a plain-string errorMessage covers every failure within its subschema
cases.description: A plain-string errorMessage replaces the library's message for any failure within its subschema.

stdout: INVALID: a record needs an id

cases.name: an object errorMessage supplies one message per failing keyword
cases.description: An object errorMessage supplies one message per failing keyword.

errorMessage.type: a record must be an object

stdout: INVALID: a record needs an id

cases.name: the object form selects the message for the keyword that actually failed
cases.description: The same schema as the previous case, failing its other keyword.

errorMessage.type: a record must be an object

stdout: INVALID: a record must be an object

cases.name: a failure no authored message covers keeps the library's own message
cases.description: A failure no authored message covers keeps each library's own message — the divergence errorMessage exists to close.

cases.name: the nearest enclosing errorMessage beats an outer one
cases.description: The lookup walks outward from the failing keyword and takes the first message it meets, so an inner message beats an outer one.

id.errorMessage: an id must be a string

stdout: INVALID: /id: an id must be a string

cases.name: an errorMessage inside a $ref'd definition covers the failure it names
cases.description: A definition factored out under $defs and applied by $ref is the ordinary way to write a schema that repeats itself, and the message belongs with the definition rather than at each referring site. The lookup has to cross the $ref boundary to find it.

errorMessage.enum: not a flavor this shop serves

stdout: INVALID: /order: not a flavor this shop serves

cases.name: an errorMessage in a --ref'd file covers a failure inside that component
cases.description: The same lookup across a file boundary rather than a pointer within one document: the message travels with the component that states the requirement.

errorMessage.enum: not a flavor this shop serves

stdout: INVALID: /order: not a flavor this shop serves

cases.name: a message inside the $ref'd definition beats one at the referring site
cases.description: Crossing the boundary does not change the rule: the lookup takes the first message it meets walking outward from the failing keyword, and the definition's own message is nearer than the one beside the $ref.

errorMessage.enum: not a flavor this shop serves

stdout: INVALID: /order: not a flavor this shop serves

cases.name: an absolute pointer interpolates the instance value at that location
cases.description: ${/a/json/pointer} interpolates the instance value at that pointer, JSON-encoded, resolved from the instance root.

artifacts.errorMessage: expected at least two artifacts, got ${/artifacts}

stdout: INVALID: /artifacts: expected at least two artifacts, got ["one"]

cases.name: a relative pointer interpolates the failing value itself
cases.description: ${0} is the failing value, wherever it occurs. Ajv binds it only where some keyword has already forced the value into a variable, which verbose mode does for every error.

items.errorMessage: each artifact must be a string; ${0} is not

stdout: INVALID: /1: each artifact must be a string; 7 is not

cases.name: a relative pointer with a path climbs from the failing value and descends again
cases.description: ${1/digest} climbs one level from the failing value and descends again.

size.errorMessage: bad size on the artifact with digest ${1/digest}

stdout: INVALID: /0/size: bad size on the artifact with digest "abc123"

cases.name: an unresolvable pointer is left as written by one leg and replaced with undefined by the other
cases.description: A pointer that does not resolve is left in the message verbatim rather than guessed at.

defect.summary: The two errorMessage implementations disagree on an unresolvable pointer: jsonschema-validate leaves ${/nonexistent/path} in the message as written, and ajv-errors substitutes the text `undefined`.
